description.value: Reduced alpha-galactosidase A activity prevents normal lysosomal clearance of Gb3 and related glycosphingolipids.

snippet.value: Fabry disease (FD) is a rare lysosomal storage disorder, characterized by a reduction in α-galactosidase A enzyme activity and the progressive accumulation of globotriaosylceramide (GL3) and its metabolites in the cells of various organs.

description.value: The shared lysosomal storage lesion occurs in multiple organ systems and must be interpreted in local tissue contexts.

snippet.value: Accumulation of GL3 in the kidney, heart, vasculature, neurons, skin, gastrointestinal tract and auditory system correlates to cellular damage and irreversible organ damage

targetName.value: Renal glycosphingolipid storage and podocyte injury

description.value: Kidney and podocyte substrate accumulation defines the renal branch and is the context for renal GL-3 tissue readouts.

snippet.value: Despite normal renal function and urinalysis, renal biopsy showed abnormal structure, with marked accumulation of GL-3 in podocytes, partial effacement of foot processes and irregularly reduced expression of nephrin in the slit diaphragm.

snippet.value: The complex pathogenesis of FD involves lysosomal dysfunction, altered autophagy, and mitochondrial abnormalities.
